references.text: 3. Mosebok describes physical requirements for priests who were to serve at the altar, including prohibitions against those with certain physical defects, reflecting the principle of holiness in the assembly.
Prohibition against offering animals with damaged testicles to the Lord, showing the same principle of physical integrity in holy contexts.
Isaiah prophesies that eunuchs who keep the Lord's Sabbath will receive a name and memorial better than sons and daughters, demonstrating God's gracious inclusion in the messianic age.
The Ethiopian court official was an eunuch who was baptized by Philip, showing that in the new covenant such restrictions are lifted through Christ.
Jesus mentions eunuchs in connection with the kingdom of heaven, showing that physical condition does not exclude one from God's kingdom in the new covenant.
Paul declares that in Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female - all barriers are removed in Christ.
